bottleneck: Tumors are mosaics of subclones with different mutations, so editing or targeting one driver leaves resistant clones to repopulate. Single-gene therapies select for escape variants, and the mutational landscape shifts during treatment, meaning the tumor sequenced at diagnosis is not the tumor being treated months later. A static genetic intervention cannot beat an evolving population without addressing heterogeneity itself, and combination approaches multiply toxicity faster than they multiply benefit.
current_state: Combination approaches and multi-target designs try to corner evolution, but tumor heterogeneity remains the primary cause of targeted-therapy failure across cancer types.

sources.title: Gene Therapy: A Breakthrough in Disease Treatment

title: Tumor heterogeneity outruns single-gene therapies
why_it_blocks: Cancer is evolution in fast-forward; single-target genetic therapies are selection pressures that breed resistance. Beating heterogeneity requires a fundamentally different strategy than adding more targets to the same paradigm.
